title: Included Miles on a Keyturn Trip Booking: Grants, Purchases and the Authority of an Odometer Reading
content:
Included miles are granted to the reservation rather than to the guest: the plan's daily allowance multiplied by the reserved days. An approved extension grants further miles at the plan's extension allowance for each extended day, granted as its own record so that the allowance of the original period and of the extension remain separable. Part packages are not sold.

Where the plan offers unlimited mileage and the vehicle sits in the Keyturn Economy Class Listing or the Keyturn Standard Class Listing value class, no allowance is metered on the reservation and no mileage record is written at all; on any higher value class the plan's daily allowance applies as usual, because unlimited mileage is not offered on vehicles the marketplace values above the standard class.

Driven miles are read from the odometer at handover and consume the allowance in the order the readings are taken. A telematics reading is authoritative where one exists; a host or guest reading stands only where no telematics reading covers the same handover, and a reading taken during a post-trip audit supersedes the reading taken at the return.

Allowance records are written only while the reservation is in the booked, in-progress or completed state, so that no allowance can be moved on a reservation that has been cancelled or closed for billing.

### Clauses of this rule that have been withdrawn

Four fragments of the wording above have been superseded by the current basis and are **no longer in force**. They are reproduced here so that no reader applies them:

| Withdrawn wording | Where it stood |
|---|---|
| "capped at the plan's per-booking ceiling however long the reservation runs" | The qualification that once closed the grant of included miles. |
| "A guest may buy further miles in whole packages only" | The opening of the clause on buying further miles. |
| "a package bought mid-trip is granted in full" | The quantity limb of that same clause. |
| "charged in full even where fewer miles are eventually driven" | The pricing limb of that same clause. |

Each of those four fragments is no longer in force.

### Which reading governs

| Readings on file for one handover | The reading that governs |
|---|---|
| A telematics reading only | The telematics reading. |
| A telematics reading and a host or guest reading | The telematics reading. |
| A host or guest reading only | That reading. |
| A return reading and a later post-trip audit reading | The audit reading. |

The order of consumption follows the order the readings are taken, not the order they reach the marketplace.

### The state gate on an allowance record

An allowance record — a grant of included miles or an odometer reading consuming them — is written only while the reservation stands in the booked, in-progress or completed state, read from the reservation's own record before the write and correlated to it by the reservation's reference number. A reservation that has been cancelled, and one that has been closed for billing, is outside those three states, which is what makes it impossible to move allowance on either.

### Unlimited mileage against the value class

*Hypothetical.* A reservation on a plan that offers unlimited mileage covers a vehicle in the Keyturn Standard Class Listing value class: no allowance is metered and no mileage record is written on that reservation at all. The same plan over a vehicle the marketplace has placed in a value class above the standard class meters the plan's daily allowance as usual, because unlimited mileage is not offered above that class.
